item.event_description: The 'Second Urbanisation' in northern India with the rise of Janapadas, Mahajanapadas, iron technology, and silver coinage.
item.source_context: Chapter 4: New Beginnings: Cities and States

stages: Rural Phase: Post-Harappan agricultural settlement (c. 1900–1000 BCE)
2nd Urbanisation: Gangetic Mahajanapadas and fortified cities (1000–500 BCE)
Imperial Urbanisation: Mauryan and Gupta capital cities (300 BCE–500 CE)

item.cause: Mastery of iron metallurgy in the 1st millennium BCE
item.effect: Allowed clearing of dense Gangetic forests and deep ploughing of alluvial clay, generating crop surplus that fueled the Second Urbanisation.
item.source_context: Chapter 4: New Beginnings: Cities and States

item.significance: The historical era (1000–500 BCE) marked by iron technology, coin usage, trade highways (Uttarapatha), and fortified capitals.
